chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Dharih al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Aqeeqa, he said: 'When seven days are exceeded, so there is no Aqeeqa for him.'

key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةِ: Aqeeqa, the ritual sacrifice offered for a newborn child
key_terms.سَبْعَةُ أَيَّامٍ: Seven days, referring to the specific time frame for the sacrifice
key_terms.لَهُ: For him, referring to the newborn child

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Aqeeqa if it is not performed on the seventh day?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the temporal limit for the Aqeeqa sacrifice, establishing that the obligation is tied specifically to the seventh day and becomes optional or discontinued if missed. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the distinction between the recommended act of shaving the head and the sacrifice, noting that while the specific timing for the seventh day is emphasized, the merit of the act remains for the child. This ruling underscores the Prophetic tradition of commemorating a newborn's arrival within the first week of life.
